title: arngz apply makes one attempt to create a space, so a cause that persists is reported once per op and cascades to every window needing it
body:
## What

hv, 10 Nov 2026, first-hand in utilz-vc's session, received by vc's date -u of 06:02Z and filed on hv's word at 06:2xZ. vc had found this while measuring issues 0133 and 0134, recorded it on 0133 as a watch item rather than filing it, and reported it to hv as a third candidate it had not filed. hv: "I'd file that and fix it as well. No point leaving a known problem lying around. Finders are fixers, remember?"

utilz 2.14.8 from Homebrew with arngz 1.1.2, on rhadamanth (macOS, the Hammerspoon engine). main at 69171b43 carries arngz 1.1.3; this defect is in both.

`arngz apply` creates a desktop space when the desk asks for one that is not there. `hs.spaces.addSpaceToScreen` can return nil with an error instead of creating it, and `exec_create_space` treats every such nil as a permanent failure: it makes **one** attempt, reports the entry `failed`, and carries on. Two consequences:

1. **The same failure is reported once per op rather than once per cause.** A condition that lasts for the whole run is reported as many times as the desk asks for a space.
2. **It cascades.** Every window the desk wanted on a space that was never created is then reported `failed` as `no_space`, which counts against apply's exit.

Run 35 in hv's log is the case: **7** create_space ops all failed with the identical reason, the user-space count never moving, and **3** windows then failed because the space they needed did not exist. One root cause, 10 failed entries, and a report in which the actual problem is stated seven times and the three windows look like separate faults.

```text
addSpaceToScreen returned nil (unable to get Mission Control data from the Dock); user spaces 4 before, 4 after
space 5 of display main does not exist, and creating it failed (its create_space result says why)
```

Repro is environmental rather than mechanical: apply a desk that needs a space created while Mission Control data cannot be read from the Dock. The behaviour under test is deterministic given a create that returns nil, which a fake can produce.

## Measured

Read first-hand by utilz-vc at main's head 69171b43, and from hv's `~/.local/state/menuz/menuz.log` (1126 lines, runs 1 to 70, 2026-10-16T19:10:59Z to 2026-11-10T05:19:53Z).

- `opt/arngz/lib/arngz.lua:341` to `:356`, `exec_create_space`: it counts the user spaces before, calls `hs.spaces.addSpaceToScreen(op.screen, true)` **once**, counts after, and returns `done` only when `ok and after == before + 1`. Every other outcome, a nil return included, is a single `failed` with the counts in the reason. There is no retry and no distinction between a transient failure and a permanent one.
- `opt/arngz/lib/plan.lua:519`: after a failed create, a window whose space does not exist is given a `no_space` op reading `space %d of display %s does not exist, and creating it failed (its create_space result says why)`, under `options.after_create`. A `no_space` op is not `unseen`, so it counts against apply's exit, which is the cascade.
- **There is already a retry helper, and this call site does not use it.** `attempts(times, f)` (`arngz.lua:85`) tries `f` up to `times` times, 200 ms apart, and three other flaky Hammerspoon reads use it as `attempts(4, ...)`: the window listing (`:120`), the running apps (`:274`) and a window read (`:287`).
- **A caution for whoever fixes this: `attempts` would not help as written.** It retries on a thrown error, through `pcall`, and `addSpaceToScreen` signals failure by *returning* `nil, err` rather than raising. Reusing `attempts` unchanged would retry nothing and silently leave the defect in place. The retry must test the returned value.
- The two reasons observed are different faults and want different answers:
  - run 35, **7 entries**, `unable to get Mission Control data from the Dock`, `user spaces 4 before, 4 after` every time. The same reason on all 7 ops of one run means the condition held for the whole run, not for an instant.
  - run 32, **1 entry**, `no display with specified id found`, `user spaces 8 before, 8 after`. That is not transient: the screen the plan named is not there, so the world has changed under the plan.
- Blast radius, counted from the log: create_space failed in 2 of the 33 `arngz apply` runs (32 and 35). In run 35 it accounts for 10 of the entries and 4 of the 6 distinct failing names (create_space itself, plus VSCode, iterm2 and Console). Neither run would be clean on this fix alone, since both also failed for other reasons, so this is not one of the 19 runs issues 0132, 0133 and 0134 would have made clean. It is filed because it is a real defect that makes a report unreadable, not because it moves that count.

## Fix

utilz-vc's recommendation, in three parts, because the two reasons are two faults:

1. **Retry a create that returns a falsy value**, bounded, in the shape of `attempts` but testing the returned value rather than only `pcall`'s success, so a genuine blip is ridden out. A new helper beside `attempts`, or `attempts` given an optional predicate, whichever keeps one home for the retry rule rather than two (Highlander).
2. **Report a persisting cause once, not once per op.** When the retry budget is spent on the first create_space op for a screen, apply stops trying to create further spaces on that screen for the rest of the run and says so in one line naming the cause and the remedy, instead of repeating an identical failure for every remaining op. The windows that needed those spaces still get their `no_space` lines, since they are true, but they point at one stated cause.
3. **Treat `no display with specified id found` as the world having changed, not as a transient.** The screen the plan named is gone, so retrying cannot help: it gets one attempt, not the retry budget, and is reported once with a reason saying the display named in the plan is no longer there.

   This was first written as "refuse before anything moves, exit 2, as `match_displays` does for a desk that does not fit", and the design narrows it, for two reasons found by reading: `M.execute` (`arngz.lua:951`) loops every op with no early exit, so stopping a run part-way would mean inventing a mechanism; and exit 2 means *refused before anything moved*, which cannot honestly be claimed once moves and places have already run. So it stays exit 1, which is true. A mid-run re-check of the world, which a real exit-2 answer would need, is a larger change and is deliberately not in this fix.

Not in this fix:

- The other failures in runs 32 and 35: Appgate's fixed size (issue 0133), Finder's and Appgate's title-bar drag refusals, and the pointer-taken-back cause. Runs 32 and 35 do not become clean on this fix.
- Whatever makes the Dock unable to serve Mission Control data. That is macOS's, and arngz's job is to ride it out where it can and say so plainly where it cannot.

**Proof.** The part with real logic, deciding whether a failure is worth retrying, is pure and is tested under plain Lua in `plan_test.lua` against the two reason strings taken from the log. The engine's coordination is read in the bytes and proved live by `acceptance.sh`, which already drives `arngz.lua` under real Hammerspoon; that is a desk run and so hv's. The design says why no new test surface is built for it: `AT-03.2` (`arngz.bats:544`) asserts `plan.lua` is pure **using `arngz.lua` as the control that must match**, so the impure engine is meant to be driven whole rather than unit-tested, and a harness stubbing the Lua `hs` namespace would be new scope against that decision.

Size S. Owner Utilz, in the same change as issues 0133 and 0134 on hv's word that there are to be no separate small releases.

**Sequencing, binding**, as on 0133 and 0134: 2.14.9's release runs (R1, R2, R3 and the tree-scan files) are pinned on 195b1c91, and the cut requires that nothing outside `intent/` has moved since that sha. This fix lands outside `intent/`. hv has ruled that all of this work goes out together rather than as separate small releases, so the pin and the release number are hv's to settle before any source edit, and the design goes in this issue first.

## Design

utilz-vc, 10 Nov 2026, ST0032/03, each file:line read at main's head 35025ba0. Size: S.

Three things found by reading shape this design, and each removes work rather than adding it.

**(a) The retry helper needs no change, and no second home.** `## Measured` warns that `attempts` (`arngz.lua:85`) retries a *thrown* error through `pcall` while `addSpaceToScreen` signals by *returning* nil, so reusing it as-is would retry nothing. The answer is not a second retry helper with a value predicate, which would put the retry rule in two homes against `IN-AG-HIGHLANDER-001`. It is to make the call raise, which is a two-line wrapper at the one call site:

```lua
local made, why = attempts(M.CREATE_SPACE_TRIES, function()
  local ok, err = hs.spaces.addSpaceToScreen(op.screen, true)
  if not ok then error(tostring(err), 0) end
  return ok
end)
```

`error(..., 0)` keeps the message clean, since level 0 adds no `file:line` prefix; without it the reason in the report would carry Lua source positions. `attempts` then gives its existing 200 ms spacing and returns `false` plus the last error, which is exactly what the reason needs. `M.CREATE_SPACE_TRIES` sits with `M.LAUNCH_TIMEOUT` as a named constant, not a literal at the call site.

**Corrected while writing it:** reusing `attempts` *entirely* unchanged turned out not to express part 3 below, that a vanished display gets one attempt rather than the budget, because `attempts` cannot be told which errors are worth waiting on. The choice was a loop of its own at this call site, duplicating the retry shape, or one optional argument on `attempts`. It took the argument: `attempts(times, f, stop)`, where `stop` is asked about an error and ends the attempts at once when it answers true. Existing callers pass no `stop` and are unaffected, and the retry rule still has one home, which was the point of not writing a second helper.

**(b) Run-scoped suppression is an idiom this file already has, twice.** `M.execute` (`arngz.lua:948`) passes one `ctx` to every exec function for the whole run, and already uses it for precisely this: it sets `ctx.unmoved[op.window]` when a move fails (`:964`), and `exec_place` reads it (`:388`) to refuse the place with "its move did not take" rather than repeating the work. `exec_create_space` is already called as `EXEC[op.op](op, ctx)` (`:957`) even though it declares only `(op)`, so it gains `ctx` with no plumbing. This fix adds `ctx.space_failed[op.screen]`, holding the first cause for that screen.

**(c) The cascade lines are true and stay.** The three `no_space` entries in run 35 come from plan, not from the engine (`plan.lua:519`, under `options.after_create`), and they correctly say the space does not exist. The issue is that the *cause* was stated seven times beside them, not that they are wrong. Nothing in plan changes.

### The change

1. **A pure classifier.** The one piece of real logic here is deciding whether a failure is worth retrying, which is a decision and so belongs in the pure core (`IN-AG-PFIC-001`), not in the engine where no suite can reach it. Add `P.space_error_kind(why)` to `plan.lua`, returning:
   - `"gone"` when the reason says the display is not there, matching Hammerspoon's `no display with specified id found`;
   - `"transient"` otherwise, which includes `unable to get Mission Control data from the Dock`.

   **Unknown reasons default to `transient` on purpose.** An unknown transient treated as permanent fails a run that would have succeeded; an unknown permanent treated as transient costs at most `CREATE_SPACE_TRIES * 200 ms` and then reports the same thing. The cheap mistake is the one to make.

2. **`exec_create_space(op, ctx)` becomes a thin coordinator** (`IN-AG-THIN-COORD-001`):
   - If `ctx.space_failed[op.screen]` is set, return `failed` at once, with a reason naming the already-stated cause and making clear it is not a fresh attempt: `creating a space on this display already failed and was not tried again (<first cause>)`. No sleeping, no call.
   - Otherwise count the user spaces before, as today.
   - Call through the wrapper in (a), but with `1` try when the first failure's kind is `"gone"`: a vanished display cannot be retried into existence. Since the kind is only known after a failure, the shape is: try once; on failure, classify; if `"transient"`, use the remaining tries; if `"gone"`, stop.
   - Count after, as today, and return `done` only when the create reported success **and** `after == before + 1`, which is today's rule and is not relaxed.
   - On final failure, set `ctx.space_failed[op.screen]` to the reason and return `failed` with today's reason text plus the counts, unchanged in wording, so a single-failure run reads exactly as it does now.

3. **What this does not do, and why.** `## Fix` part 3 proposed refusing with exit 2 for the vanished-display case, "as `match_displays` already refuses a desk that does not fit". That is narrowed here, and the issue's `## Fix` is corrected to match rather than left contradicting the design. Two reasons: `M.execute` (`:951`) loops every op with no early exit, so there is no mechanism to stop a run part-way without inventing one; and exit 2 means *refused before anything moved*, which cannot honestly be claimed once moves and places have already run. So the vanished display stays exit 1, which is true, and is reported once with a reason that says the display named in the plan is no longer there. A mid-run re-check of the world, which is what a real exit-2 answer would need, is a larger change and is deliberately not in this fix.

### What changes, and what the counts become

Run 35 under this fix: the first create_space op tries up to `CREATE_SPACE_TRIES` times, 200 ms apart, and if the Dock is still unreadable it fails once with the cause. The remaining six return immediately pointing at it. The three windows keep their `no_space` lines. So the report carries one stated cause instead of seven, and apply does six fewer rounds of work. Run 35 still exits 1, and the issue says so: it also failed for Appgate, Finder and the pointer, so this fix alone does not make it clean.

### Tests, red at the base and green at the fix

The pure part is fully covered; the engine part is not reachable by any suite, which is why as much as possible is pure.

- `plan_test.lua`: `P.space_error_kind` returns `"gone"` for Hammerspoon's exact `no display with specified id found` string, taken from run 32's log line rather than invented; `"transient"` for run 35's exact `unable to get Mission Control data from the Dock`; `"transient"` for an empty string and for an unrecognised message, which pins the deliberate default.
- `plan_test.lua`: the existing `apply_report` check at `:955`, which already renders a failed `create_space`, keeps its answer. That is the regression guard that the report side is untouched.
- **The engine's coordination is not given a new test surface, and `## Fix`'s promise of fake-driven arms is corrected here.** vc first planned a fake `hs.spaces` driving `exec_create_space` directly, then read the suites and found that would mean a harness loading `arngz.lua` with a stubbed `hs`, which nothing does today: `plan_test.lua` dofiles `plan.lua` alone, and `arngz.bats` fakes the `hs` *command-line tool* at the shim, not the Lua `hs` namespace. Building one is new scope, and the project has already decided this split deliberately: `AT-03.2` (`arngz.bats:544`) asserts `plan.lua` makes no `hs`, `io`, `os` or `require` call, **using `arngz.lua` as the control that the pattern does match**, so `arngz.lua` is impure by design and is meant to be driven whole, not unit-tested.

  So the engine's two coordination lines are proved the way 0132's amended design proved its engine change, which hv accepted: the decision is pure and tested above, the coordination is small enough to read in the bytes, and the live proof is `acceptance.sh` (`opt/arngz/test/acceptance.sh:75`), which already runs `arngz.lua` under real Hammerspoon. That is a desk run and so is hv's, not this session's.

  Keeping the split also means the one new function in `plan.lua`, `P.space_error_kind`, must stay pure string matching with no `hs`, `io`, `os` or `require`, or `AT-03.2` goes red. That is a free regression guard on this change and is why the classifier is written the way it is.

No expected count is written by hand in any of these: each check asserts its own outcome.

### Docs and runs

`help/arngz.md`: apply's account of creating a space says a failure is retried and that a cause which persists is stated once per display. The CHANGELOG's `[2.14.9] - unreleased` gains a Fixed entry. arngz's version is set once for the whole release.

No run this session may start (vc decision 74; the desk is agentic-engineering-vc's). The smallest run that proves the change (vc decision 67) is `plan_test.lua` under plain Lua plus the fake-driven arms above, and they need hv's own run or a desk grant.
